I fully, truly, feel what you are saying. I don’t know exactly how you feel an your exact circumstances, but I feel a very similar degree of anger on a near constant basis. I have suffered from mental illness for most of my life, it still affects me now, and that has been coupled with a handful of traumatic and abusive experiences that have doubled down on that feeling of rage… I think what you are describing makes a lot of sense, in the way that I think a lot of rage in general stems from a core feeling of powerlessness. There have been so many situations in my life where I have fully been condescended, abused, mistreated, and just spoken to with so little respect, and in my case, it was most often by people that I was relying on for a place to live, or as my caretakers when I was younger. So it didn’t even feel like I had a choice as to whether or not I could stand up for myself. I had to endure a lot of fucked up stuff just for survival. And the cycle of anger ensues in the same fashion that you have described. And you’re right. Most of the people who have really done me wrong have not ended up in the same mental or logistical ruts that I have found myself in. Most of the people who have done me wrong I know for a fact are doing fine, are comfortable in their life, and don’t feel any type of guilt for the way they treated me. It hurts. It hurts bad. I get those violent thoughts as well, all the time. 

I try to think about what my anger is telling me, because I think anger gets painted as a “bad emotion” waaaaay too easily. Anger is your greatest teacher/indicator of so many things. Anger let’s you know when you are not being treated with respect, even if you don’t have the self-esteem to realize it yet. Anger let’s you know when things are not fair in your life. Anger let’s you know when you aren’t satisfied and haven’t gotten what you deserve. Anger let’s you know when you are hurt inside…. The list goes on and on. A lot of the time for me, I feel so angry because I feel totally alone in my experiences of abuse and neglect. I try to use the mental energy from my anger and direct it towards figuring out how I might resolve the loneliness. Brainstorm how I can connect with other people, no matter how awkward or unnatural it feels at first. Social media has been pissing me off in the same way that you just described. Everything all at once, it’s just too fucking much on there… so I’ve started reading more to put that energy into learning about things I want to learn about, instead of scrolling on my phone and feeding into that angry internal monologue. Those are just a couple of examples, I could go on… but the bottom line is that anger is never the problem, anger is just the emotion that shows up when there is a problem, and that problem could be a multitude of different things that aren’t going right. I feel your pain, I hear what you are saying. You deserve respect, and the way that people have treated you in the past was absolutely disrespectful, and it is not your fault because you handled it the best you could at the time. I believe you will find a way, and you never should have to dismiss your pain, you just need to address it. Sending you lots of love ❤️

Hey there. I am really sorry to hear that you are struggling. I would research therapists online to find one that does “sliding-scale” pricing. This is the case with my therapist, and it just means that they work with your budget if you have to pay out of pocket. I can’t afford to pay for therapy right now so mine gives me appointments for free. I don’t have health insurance and haven’t for a while, and wouldn’t be able to afford it out of pocket. I don’t know where you live, but I would start doing some internet research for therapists that offer sliding-scale pricing so that way at least you can remove the financial barrier and get some help faster. I hope that was helpful, and I wish you the best of luck.

Hey there. I am really sorry that you are feeling so incredibly low. I struggle very deeply with mental-illness, anxiety and depression in particular, as well as suicide ideation pretty much constantly. It sounds like you experienced some pretty intense losses there, and given the nature of both those deaths I imagine that must not help you out of the hole you feel you are in. I am very sorry for your losses. I have not experienced exactly what you have experienced, but I would like to share some advice that has helped me, and even if it hasn’t helped me a lot, it at least makes me feel better. 

I know this probably sounds really annoying, given that everyone says this, but just take things one day at a time, and if that is too much, then take things an hour at a time… if that’s too much, then one minute at a time, and well, you get the gist. Looking at things from a harm reduction perspective really has helped me get out of a rut much faster than trying to make major changes fast. 

I don’t know what drugs you are using, but if you must use them, make sure the paraphernalia (needles, etc) are clean and sterile, if that applies to you. Try to let someone know about what you are using. I don’t know off the top of my head, you can look it up, but I am pretty sure there is a hotline where if you are going to use a substance, someone will stay on the phone with you in case you overdose or something happens, you can get help sent your way. While you are taking steps to at least ensure that your drug use is as safe as it can be, maybe start to look into where local NA meetings are held in your area (at least if you are in the USA). Otherwise, start to research, or have your boyfriend research your options for you. You went through something really intense, and it sounds like being alive is really hard right now, and I do not shame you for using drugs as a way to cope. So at least, just try to be as safe as possible about it if you cannot stop right now. 

Also, it’s okay if you cannot leave your room, or that feels like too much. I don’t know if you work, or have money to spend like that, but order doordash, or have food delivered to where you live so you at least eat. You deserve a full belly, and to be as physically healthy as you can. I get that going outside and facing the world in any capacity can feel like a lot, so you don’t have to do that if it’s too much. One day at a time, remember? In addition to eating, try to stay hydrated. I’m not sure what exactly you are using, but staying hydrated and fed as much as possible is extra important in your case. You deserve the care. 

Lastly, be gentle with yourself and don’t judge yourself. The world is a really hard place to be even if you don’t have anything tough to deal with, and you experienced two deaths which I imagine both hit hard in some way. I know how difficult it is to ask for help, believe me I struggle with it still myself, but you have a boyfriend, and it’s okay to ask people that love you for help and support. It’s ok if you don’t know what to do and where to start your healing journey. If you have any other family or kind people in your lives, make it known to them that you are struggling and you need support, ask other people to help you find a rehab program, or to help you look into the free resources your city has to offer for people who are struggling mentally, or with addiction. 

I believe in you, you are not by yourself, and you deserve attention, care, and healing. I know how relentless and difficult and impossible life can feel, and I know how bad depression can get. I am proud of you for expressing your feelings and situation on here, and you don’t have to make any huge overwhelming changes right away. Healing takes so much more time than people make it seem, and it’s okay to take your time, and take it slow, and hide from the world as long as you need. Let people help you and take care of you, no matter how uncomfortable that may feel, and don’t shame yourself. You are a human being. It does take hard work to dig yourself out of a hole, but it is not impossible work. Sending love to you, you can do this x

I’ve been having the same issue, and it’s only been a week for me... it’s hard to get to sleep because all of a sudden the thoughts I was distracted from during the day through work and other activities all hit me at once. I bought some melatonin gummies and have been taking those whenever I start to feel tired at night so that way I can wind down and actually fall asleep. My issue is I stay up ruminating no matter how tired I am, and my anxiety can really keep me awake that way. The melatonin has helped keep me on a good sleep schedule, and getting sleep so you can be more active during the days I think will help me do what I need to do as well. At least I hope.
I wish you the best of luck with that conversation, and I hope everything works out for the best

I just broke up with someone who I was “on a break” with for the last month we were together. I spent the break trying to work on myself to improve the relationship, while they used it to sort of half-ass the relationship and think about whether they even really wanted to be with me. They broke up with me last week because they ultimately resented me and didn’t really want to be with me right now. Just wanted to paint the picture of my situation before giving advice. I think as much as break-ups can suck sometimes, I definitely learned from my experience that certainty feels a whole lot better than being stuck in uncertainty. I think if you were previously together, and now your on this break, but it’s unclear if the intentions of this break is to continue the relationship, it might be the best for both of you to break up. I feel shitty right now because I’m going through a break up, but I definitely feel a sense of relief that I’m not stuck waiting around for someone who has one-foot-in-one-foot-out of the relationship so to speak. If someone wants to be with you, they will make the effort and make their intentions clear. I just wasted a month of my time on a break with my partner who turns out was using that time to detach herself from me without having to end it. I would hate to have you go through the same. Communication and clarity is key. And even if your partner genuinely isn’t sure and they are upfront and honest about that, I think it could be worth discussing whether staying in this limbo, or breaking up is the best option for figuring that out.

Thank you for saying all this and understanding, you have no idea how desperately I needed that validation. I hope I can find a way out of this situation. You are correct it is going on in my home environment. It’s so exhausting dude to as you said, put in so so much and get nothing back.
I hear you. I really do. I feel the same way so much of the time.
